prior_upstream_pin.title: ble: ask again for the peripheral once the radio is up, instead of scanning for one already bonded (#2436)
prior_upstream_pin.body:
ble: ask again for the peripheral once the radio is up, instead of scanning for one already bonded (#2436)

Reported in #2433 by @pipiche38, with the root cause and the remedy already
traced. Every claim was checked against the source rather than the trace, and
there was one more door than the report names.

`retrievePeripherals(withIdentifiers:)` answers nothing before `.poweredOn`.
Every source read that empty answer as "this device has never been seen here"
and took the discovery branch: park the id, arm a service-filtered scan. The
replay on `.poweredOn` then looked the id up in `seenPeripherals` only, which
is empty for the same reason, so it fell through to the scan it had just armed.
The targeted connect CoreBluetooth honours while the app is suspended was never
issued.

In the foreground this costs nothing: a scan finds the device in 1-6 s. In the
background iOS throttles scanning hard. The report has a Gen3 ring bonded to
the phone for weeks found 29 min 54 s after a background relaunch, and 4 min
31 s earlier the same day, beside a WHOOP central that attached immediately.
Every launch printed "not cached yet", 8 of 8 in that export, for a ring that
plainly was.

BLEManager already learned this for straps in #2272, where the comment reads
"a background scan would not find it". The four peripheral sources never did.

Two doors, not one. `issueStandingConnect` carries the same conflation, and it
is worse there, because its fallback calls `connect(id)`, which scans. Scanning
is the one thing a standing connect exists to avoid, against its own promise
that CoreBluetooth reconnects "whenever the ring is reachable, including while
the app is suspended".

Both entry points now park the intent before the retrieve when the state is not
`.poweredOn`, which also stops the log claiming something the code never
checked. The replay re-issues the retrieve, now that an empty answer means
something, and connects what it finds.

Parking means nothing calls `scan()` on the way past, so a parked connect that
still cannot be resolved has no deferred scan to pick up: it arms discovery
itself rather than answering "nothing to do", which would drop a first-ever
pairing in silence. Four outcomes, not three, and `didDiscover` still connects
the parked id on sight.

Same change in the three sibling sources carrying the identical block:
StandardHRSource, HuamiHRSource, FTMSSource. BLEManager was checked and is
clean throughout, guarding the state before every retrieve.

The decision is extracted as `PendingConnect.replay`, a pure function of
(parked, held, retrieved, scanning), testable without a radio, a peripheral or
a CBCentralManager, as the report suggested. Eight cases in StrandTests, two of
them invariants over the whole input space: a parked connect is never dropped,
and nothing is ever started for a caller who asked for nothing. Mutation-tested
twice, each reddening only what it should.

Android needs no twin: `getRemoteDevice(address)` rehydrates from a stable MAC
whatever the adapter state, while CoreBluetooth's per-app UUIDs need the radio
up to resolve.

What no unit test covers is the hardware half, which is the acceptance signal
the report names: a background relaunch followed within seconds by a connect
line rather than a scan.

Refs #1213, #1215
